title: 📰 AI news · November 19
takeaway: Two stories about access today: US banks wrote into their terms that you answer for what a connected AI agent does, and Irish credit unions lost customer data through a contractor. Recommendation: list which accounts and services your agents and bots are connected to, and make sure anything that moves money needs your confirmation.

items.title: US banks: you answer for your AI agent
items.text: Citibank, PNC and Citizens now say in their terms: if you give an AI agent access to your account, the bank does not have to reverse its transactions, even accidental ones. If the tool leaks credentials or is hacked, you are responsible for what the attackers do. JPMorgan and Bank of America adopted similar rules last month. If your agent or bot can touch money, it acts in your name. Check what access it has and what it does without your confirmation.

items.title: Data of 40 Irish credit unions exposed
items.text: A script sent about 5 million requests through the IT contractor Wellington IT and pulled saved payee data: names, IBANs, account numbers and addresses. Passwords, PINs and card data were not affected. Your customers' data also sits with contractors, such as payment and CRM services. Find out what data third-party services of your project hold.

items.title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.text: A fast model for code and agents: one million tokens of context, $3 per million input tokens and $15 for output, half that in batch mode. It aims at Gemini 4 Carbon quality with more speed and lower cost.

items.title: HeyGen releases Avatar 6
items.text: A video of you from one photo and a voice recording, every frame in 2K. In HeyGen's own tests, viewers picked the result as real 42.2% of the time. A faster Turbo version is available.

items.title: Google's AI Mode gets an incognito
items.text: A temporary thread opens a conversation that stays out of your search history and recommendations. It rolls out worldwide on desktop and mobile.

items.title: Anthropic prices its shares at $83
items.text: TechCrunch reports the price is above the $70–78 range and values the company at $1.5 trillion. Trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT starts on Thursday.

items.title: Snapchat lenses can be built with words
items.text: Easy Lens CLI: you describe a lens, and Claude Code, Cursor or Codex build, test and publish it. Creators in Lens+ Payouts were paid $1.8 million last month.
